summary: This is a reference page for the TRIM string function, which removes leading and trailing characters from a string. If no characters are specified, it removes leading and trailing blank spaces by default. The page covers syntax, arguments, usage notes about explicitly specifying whitespace characters, collation behavior, and two SQL examples.
one_line: Reference documentation for the TRIM string function, which strips specified leading and trailing characters (default: spaces) from a string.
key_facts: TRIM(<expr> [, <characters> ]) removes leading and trailing characters from a string expression.
The default value of the characters argument is a single blank space character ' '.
If no characters are specified, all leading and trailing blank spaces are removed.
The characters in the characters argument can be specified in any order.
To remove whitespace, the whitespace characters must be explicitly included in the argument.
TRIM('$.') removes leading and trailing blank spaces, dollar signs, and periods from the input string.
TRIM does not remove other whitespace characters such as tabulation characters or end-of-line characters unless explicitly specified.
Collation is supported when the optional second argument is omitted, or when it contains only constant whitespace.
The collation specification of the returned value is the same as the collation specification of the first argument.
The second example uses CONCAT with '>' and '<' to visualize whitespace removal from the tr table.
In the whitespace example, TRIM applied to '  asd  ' yields '>asd<'.
TRIM applied to a NULL value returns NULL.
The page is listed under the Functions-String reference section and the language shown is English.
